learn.hook: The sun rises in the East every morning. Can you use it to find North, South and West? Let's become explorers!
points: The four main directions are North, South, East and West.
If you face North, East is on your right, West is on your left and South is behind you.
The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.
Between the main directions are North-East, North-West, South-East and South-West.
A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise. A left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise.

example.q: Meena faces North. She turns right, and then turns right again. Which way is she facing now?

learn.reallife: Taxi drivers, pilots, ship captains and scouts all use directions.

items.text: Facing North, your left hand points ___

games.title: True or false?
items: If you face East, North is on your left.
Facing East, turning left (anticlockwise) takes you to North.
If you face South, East is on your right.
Facing South, West is on your right and East is on your left.
Turning right two times from North makes you face South.
North → East → South.
North-West is between North and West.
Its name tells you: North + West.
Turning from East to South is a left turn.
East to South is clockwise, so it is a right turn.

quiz.q: You are facing North. Which direction is on your right?
quiz.explain: Facing North, East is on your right.

quiz.q: Kabir faces East and turns left. Which way does he face now?
quiz.explain: A left turn is anticlockwise. From East, anticlockwise goes to North.

quiz.q: In which direction does the sun rise?
quiz.explain: The sun rises in the East every morning.

quiz.q: Arjun walks 3 blocks North, then 2 blocks East, then 3 blocks South. Where is he now compared with his start?
quiz.explain: The 3 blocks North and 3 blocks South cancel out. He is 2 blocks East of his start.

quiz.q: Harpreet faces West and turns right. Which way does she face now?
quiz.explain: A right turn is clockwise. From West, clockwise goes to North.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a right turn always leads to East

quiz.q: Which direction is halfway between North and East?
quiz.explain: Halfway between North and East is North-East.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of the in-between directions

quiz.q: Riya walks 4 blocks East and then 4 blocks West. How many blocks is she from where she started?
quiz.explain: East and West are opposite. 4 − 4 = 0, so she is back at the start.
quiz.mistake: Adds the blocks instead of seeing the walks cancel

quiz.q: Joseph faces North and turns until he faces South. How many degrees did he turn?
quiz.explain: North to South is a half turn, which is 180°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is a quarter turn

quiz.q: Early in the morning Kabir stands facing the rising Sun. Which direction is on his left?
quiz.explain: The Sun rises in the East, so he faces East. With East in front, North is on the left, South on the right and West behind.
steps: Facing the rising Sun = facing East
quiz.mistake: Mixes up left and right when facing East

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'I am facing North. Where are East, West and South?'
teach.praise: Hooray! East on my right, West on my left and South behind me. Now I won't get lost!
teach.nudge: Which direction is on my right hand? Which one is behind me?

topics.title: Bird watching: directions from a landmark

learn.hook: Kites are seen to the north of the lake, ducks to the east. Can you mark them on the map?
points: A landmark is a place everyone can find, like a lake, temple or big tree.
We describe where something is by its direction from the landmark: 'The heron is south of the lake.'
On a map with North at the top: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left.
To draw an object 'to the west of the lake', draw it on the left side of the lake.
Read every clue and place the objects one by one.

example.q: On a map, the lake is in the middle. A peacock is to the east of the lake. Where do you draw it?
example.answer: To the right of the lake

learn.reallife: Bird watchers at Bharatpur's Keoladeo park describe sightings using directions from lakes and trees.

games.title: Where on the map? (North at top)
Bird map
items: If the kingfisher is drawn to the right of the lake, it is east of the lake.
With North at the top, right is east.
A heron south of the lake is drawn above it.
South is below.
If the tree is west of the lake, the lake is east of the tree.
Directions swap when you switch the landmark.
A crane drawn above the lake is to its north.
Up is north.

quiz.q: On a map with North at the top, a stork is drawn above the lake. Which direction is it from the lake?
quiz.explain: Above means north on such a map.

quiz.q: Ducks are to the west of the lake. Where should Riya draw them?
options: To the left of the lake
To the right of the lake
quiz.explain: West is to the left when North is at the top.

quiz.q: A peacock is drawn to the right of the lake. Which direction is it from the lake?
quiz.explain: Right is east on a map with North at the top.

quiz.q: The banyan tree is east of the lake. Which direction is the lake from the tree?
quiz.explain: If A is east of B, then B is west of A.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the same direction when switching landmarks

quiz.q: Clues: the parrot is north of the lake, and the owl is south of the parrot but north of the lake. Where is the owl?
options: Between the parrot and the lake
quiz.explain: South of the parrot and north of the lake puts it between them.
quiz.mistake: Uses only one of the clues

quiz.q: A heron is below the lake on the map. Which direction is it from the lake?
quiz.explain: Below means south.

quiz.q: Kites are to the north-east of the lake. Where on the map?
options: Up and to the right of the lake
quiz.explain: North is up and east is right.

quiz.q: Which is the best landmark to describe where a bird is?
quiz.explain: A landmark must stay in one place.

teach.ask: Gappu saw a crane to the south of the lake. Where should I draw it on our map (North at the top)?
teach.praise: South is down, so I draw the crane below the lake!
teach.nudge: Which way is south on our map?

learn.hook: Draw your room from above, like a bird looking down. Where is your bed? Your window? Your door?
points: We can say where things are from a person's view: 'The cupboard is to Ravi's left.'
With directions, we say: 'The window is on the north wall.'
A room map is drawn from above. Draw an arrow showing North on it.
List the objects on each side: north wall, south wall, east wall, west wall.
Use simple shapes for objects: a rectangle for a bed, a square for a table.

example.q: Ravi stands in his room facing north. The window is in front of him and the door is behind him. On which walls are they?
example.answer: Window on the north wall, door on the south wall

learn.reallife: Architects draw room plans from above with a North arrow, so builders know which way windows face.

games.title: Facing north: which wall?
items: Straight ahead
Behind you
On your right
On your left
In front of you
At your back

items.text: A room map is drawn as seen from ___
A map needs an arrow to show ___
Facing north, your right hand points ___
Facing north, your left hand points ___

quiz.q: Meena faces north in her room. The bed is on her right. Which wall is the bed near?
quiz.explain: Facing north, right is east.

quiz.q: Facing north, the cupboard is behind Arjun. Which side of the room is it?
quiz.explain: Behind is the opposite of in front: south.

quiz.q: Why do we draw a North arrow on a room map?
options: To show the size of the room
So anyone can tell the directions on the map
To show where the door is
quiz.explain: The arrow lets readers know which way is north, so they can work out the other directions.

quiz.q: From which view is a room map drawn?
quiz.explain: Maps show places as seen from above.
quiz.mistake: Draws it like a side picture

quiz.q: Sara faces east. The window is on her left. Which wall is the window on?
quiz.explain: Facing east, left is north.
quiz.mistake: Uses the 'facing north' rule for every direction

quiz.q: On Kabir's room map, the table is near the west wall. If North is at the top of the map, where is the table drawn?
quiz.explain: West is on the left of a map with North at the top.
quiz.mistake: Thinks west is on the right

quiz.q: In a room, the door is on the south wall and the window on the north wall. Which is true?
options: They are on the same wall
The door is on the east wall
The window is opposite the door
The window is next to the door
quiz.explain: North and south walls face each other.

quiz.q: Which list correctly names objects to the east of Riya if the bed is east, the desk is west and the shelf is east?
quiz.explain: The bed and the shelf are both on the east side.

teach.ask: Gappu is drawing a map of his nest-room. What must I put on it so others can read the directions?
teach.praise: I draw it from above with a North arrow, and simple shapes for things!
teach.nudge: What helps readers know which way is north?

learn.hook: The school bus goes from Ravi's house to the zoo. Turn left, go straight, turn right… can you follow it?
points: Describe a route with directions, turns (left/right) and road names: 'Go north on Gandhi Road, turn right into Nehru Road.'
A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise; a left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise.
To find places in a direction from a house, look on that side of the house on the map.
Trace a route on a map with your finger or a pencil, stop by stop.
To decide which stop is nearer, count blocks or compare distances.

example.q: Ravi walks north on Gandhi Road and turns right into Nehru Road. Which direction is he walking now?

learn.reallife: Bus drivers, delivery riders and taxi drivers follow routes with turns every day.

games.title: Follow the route
games.prompt: Ravi's route: north on Gandhi Road, right into Nehru Road past the post office, then left into Park Street to the zoo gate. Put the steps in order.
items: Leave home on Gandhi Road going north
Turn right into Nehru Road
Pass the post office
Turn left into Park Street
Reach the zoo gate

quiz.q: Ravi walks north and turns right. Which way is he walking now?
quiz.explain: A right turn from north is a quarter turn clockwise: east.

quiz.q: The bus goes east and turns left. Which way is it going now?
quiz.explain: A left turn from east is anticlockwise: north.

quiz.q: A map shows the park to the north of Sita's house and the market to the south. Which is north of her house?
quiz.explain: The park lies on the north side.

quiz.q: The zoo is 3 blocks from stop A and 5 blocks from stop B. Which stop is nearer?
quiz.explain: 3 blocks is less than 5 blocks.

quiz.q: Going south on MG Road, the bus turns right into Lake Road. Which way is it going?
quiz.explain: Right from south is clockwise: west.
quiz.mistake: Uses the turn rule for facing north

quiz.q: To get from home to school, you go 2 blocks east then 3 blocks north. To come back the same way, what is the first move?
quiz.explain: Retrace the last move first, in the opposite direction.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the route instead of reversing it

quiz.q: The temple is east of the bus stop and the zoo is west of it. Kiran is at the bus stop. Which way should she walk to the zoo?
quiz.explain: The zoo is to the west of the stop.

quiz.q: What does 'trace a route on a map' mean?
options: Count the colours on the map
Follow the path from start to end, marking each road and turn
quiz.explain: Tracing shows the whole path step by step.
quiz.mistake: Thinks tracing means copying the map

teach.ask: Gappu flies north and then turns left. Which way am I flying now?
teach.praise: From north, a left turn is anticlockwise to west!
teach.nudge: Which way does a left turn go: clockwise or anticlockwise?

learn.hook: Imagine you are a bird flying over your town. What you see from up there is what a map shows!
points: A map is a drawing of a place as seen from above (a bird's-eye view).
A map is much smaller than the real place.
The key (legend) tells what each symbol on the map means.
Most maps have North at the top.
Grid maps use a letter for the column and a number for the row, like B4, to find places quickly.

example.q: On a grid map, columns are A to E (left to right) and rows are 1 to 5 (top to bottom). The temple is in column C, row 2. How do we name its square?
steps: Write the column letter first: C

learn.reallife: Maps help us find a shop in a mall, a platform at a railway station or a route on a phone.

games.title: True or false?
items: A map is a drawing of a place seen from above.
It is like a bird's-eye view.
A map key tells us what the symbols mean.
For example, 🌳 might stand for a park.
A map shows things bigger than they really are.
A map shrinks a place so it fits on paper.
On most maps, North is at the bottom.
On most maps, North is at the top.
Grid squares like B2 help us find places on a map.
The letter gives the column and the number gives the row.

quiz.q: On a map, what does the key (legend) tell us?
quiz.explain: The key explains the symbols, like 🏫 for a school.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the key and guesses what symbols mean

quiz.q: A map shows a place as it looks from…
quiz.explain: A map is a bird's-eye view, as if looking down from above.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of a picture taken from the side

quiz.q: On most maps, which direction is at the top?
quiz.explain: Most maps put North at the top.

quiz.q: On a grid map, the school is in column B, row 4. Which square is it in?
quiz.explain: Column letter first, then row number: B4.

quiz.q: On a grid map, Arjun's house is in A1 and the market is in A4, in the same column. How many squares down is the market from his house?
quiz.explain: From row 1 to row 4 is 4 − 1 = 3 squares.

quiz.q: A map shows a whole city on one page. Compared with the real city, the map is…
quiz.explain: A map shrinks the real place so it fits on paper.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a map is drawn at real size

quiz.q: Which is the best landmark to tell a friend the way to your house?
options: A big red temple at the corner
quiz.explain: A landmark should be big and stay in one place. Clouds, bicycles and dogs move!

quiz.q: On a grid map, rows are numbered 1 at the top to 5 at the bottom. The park is in C3. Which square is just above it?
quiz.explain: Moving up one row in the same column: row 3 → row 2. So C2.
quiz.mistake: Moves along the row instead of up, or goes down

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a map? How do I know what the little pictures mean?'
teach.praise: Wow! A map is a bird's-eye drawing, and the key tells what each symbol means. Just like my view!
teach.nudge: From where is a map drawn? What tells me the meaning of each symbol?

learn.hook: A metro map uses coloured lines. Where two lines meet, you can change trains — that is an interchange!
points: Each metro line has a colour and a list of stations in order.
An interchange station is where two lines meet. You change trains there.
Example map — Red Line: Anand, Bagh, City Centre, Dairy, Eastgate. Blue Line: Fort, Ganga, City Centre, Hill, Ishan.
To go from Anand to Hill: Red Line to City Centre (change), then Blue Line to Hill.
Count the stations to choose the route with the fewest stops.

example.q: Using the map above, how many stops from Anand to Hill?
steps: Change to Blue: City Centre → Hill (3)

learn.reallife: The Delhi Metro has many coloured lines like Yellow, Blue and Violet with interchange stations like Rajiv Chowk.

games.title: Our metro map
pairs: Last station listed on Red Line
Last station listed on Blue Line
First station listed on Red Line
First station listed on Blue Line

quiz.q: Red Line: Anand, Bagh, City Centre, Dairy, Eastgate. Blue Line: Fort, Ganga, City Centre, Hill, Ishan. Which is the interchange?
quiz.explain: City Centre is on both lines.
quiz.mistake: Picks a station on only one line

quiz.q: On that map, how many stops from Anand to Eastgate on the Red Line?
quiz.explain: Anand → Bagh → City Centre → Dairy → Eastgate: 4 stops.

quiz.q: To go from Bagh to Hill, where must you change trains?
quiz.explain: Bagh is on Red and Hill is on Blue; they meet at City Centre.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every trip needs no change

quiz.q: How many stops from Fort to Dairy?
quiz.explain: Fort → Ganga → City Centre (2), change, → Dairy (3).

quiz.q: Which line would you take from Ganga to Ishan?
quiz.explain: Ganga and Ishan are both on the Blue Line.

quiz.q: A legend on a metro map shows ● for a station and ◎ for an interchange. What does ◎ at City Centre tell you?
quiz.explain: The legend says ◎ means interchange.

quiz.q: Tina can go Anand → City Centre → Hill (3 stops) or ride to Eastgate and take a bus (6 stops' time). Which is better to reach Hill fast?
options: The metro route via City Centre
quiz.explain: Fewer stops usually means less time.

quiz.q: How many different stations are on this whole map (Red and Blue lines)?
quiz.explain: 5 on Red + 5 on Blue = 10, but City Centre is counted twice: 9.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to go from Bagh to Ishan on our metro map. Which route and where do I change?
teach.praise: Red Line to City Centre, then change to the Blue Line to Ishan!
teach.nudge: Which lines are Bagh and Ishan on?

topics.title: Making a school map and a treasure hunt

learn.hook: Hide a treasure in your school and draw a map so your friends can find it!
points: A school map shows buildings and places from above: classrooms, playground, office, library.
Make a key: choose a simple symbol for each place (□ classroom, ✚ first aid, 🌳 tree).
Draw a North arrow and keep places in the right positions compared with each other.
For a treasure hunt, mark the hidden object with ✖ and give direction clues: '10 steps east of the tap.'
Check your map by asking a friend to follow it.

example.q: Your map key says ▲ = water tap. A ✖ is drawn just east of ▲. Where is the treasure?
steps: East is to the right on a map with North at the top
example.answer: Just to the east of the water tap

learn.reallife: Scouts and guides make maps with keys for camps and treasure hunts.

games.title: Make a treasure map
items: Walk around and list the places
Draw them from above in the right positions
Add symbols and a key
Draw a North arrow
Mark the treasure with ✖ and write clues

quiz.q: Why does a school map need a key?
options: To show what each symbol means
quiz.explain: The key explains the symbols used.

quiz.q: Which is the best symbol for the school library?
options: A big red circle with no label
quiz.explain: A symbol should remind readers of the place and be listed in the key.

quiz.q: The treasure is '10 steps north of the big tree'. On a map with North at the top, where is it drawn?
quiz.explain: North is up.

quiz.q: Ria hid a ball west of the office. On the map (North at top), which side of the office is ✖?
quiz.explain: West is on the left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks west is on the right

quiz.q: Which clue is the most helpful for finding hidden treasure?
options: 5 steps east of the water tap
quiz.explain: It gives a landmark, a direction and a distance.

quiz.q: What must every good school map have?
options: A key and a North arrow
quiz.explain: The key explains symbols and the arrow gives direction.

quiz.q: Your friend follows your map but cannot find the treasure. What is the best thing to do?
options: Check the positions and clues on the map
quiz.explain: Checking helps find the mistake in the map or clues.

quiz.q: The office is east of the library and the playground is east of the office. Which is farthest east?
quiz.explain: Library → office → playground going east.

teach.ask: Gappu hid a worm treasure 3 hops south of the swing. How do I show it on our school map?
teach.praise: I find the swing, go down 3 hops, and mark ✖ there!
teach.nudge: Which way is south on the map?

learn.hook: An ant walks 2 cm north and 3 cm east to reach the sugar. Is there more than one way? Which is shortest?
points: On a grid, describe moves with distance and direction: '2 cm north, then 3 cm east'.
There can be many routes to the same point: 3 cm east then 2 cm north also works.
The shortest routes along grid lines never go backwards. For 2 north and 3 east, every shortest route is 5 cm.
A route that goes south and then north again is longer.
To return home, reverse the moves: 3 cm west, then 2 cm south.

example.q: An ant goes 4 cm east, 1 cm north, 2 cm west and 1 cm north. How far is it from the start, and in which directions?
example.answer: 2 cm east and 2 cm north of the start

learn.reallife: Delivery riders look for the shortest route through the lanes of a town, just like the ant!

games.title: Ant routes
items: 2 cm north then 3 cm east reaches the same point as 3 cm east then 2 cm north.
Both end 3 east and 2 north.
The shortest route along the grid to 2 north and 3 east is 5 cm.
Going 1 cm south first can still give a 5 cm route to that point.
It must come back north, adding 2 cm.
To go back home after 2 north and 3 east, go 3 west and 2 south.
Reverse each move.

quiz.q: An ant walks 2 cm north and then 3 cm east. How far does it walk?
Which route reaches the same point as '2 cm north, 3 cm east'?
quiz.explain: Both end 3 cm east and 2 cm north of the start.

quiz.q: Route A: 2 N, 3 E. Route B: 1 S, 3 N, 3 E. Which is shorter?
quiz.mistake: Thinks every route to a point is the same length

quiz.q: What is the shortest grid route length to a point 3 cm north and 4 cm east?
quiz.explain: Shortest routes never go backwards: 3 + 4 = 7 cm.

quiz.q: An ant walks 4 cm east, 1 cm north, 2 cm west and 1 cm north. Where is it from the start?
quiz.explain: East − west = 4 − 2 = 2 cm east. North = 1 + 1 = 2 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds east and west instead of subtracting

quiz.q: After going 2 cm north and 3 cm east, how can the ant go straight back home along the grid?
quiz.explain: Undo each move in the opposite direction.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the moves instead of reversing them

quiz.q: Which route is NOT a shortest route to 1 cm north and 2 cm east?
options: 1 cm east, 1 cm north, 1 cm east
1 cm west, 1 cm north, 3 cm east
quiz.explain: It goes west first, so it is 5 cm long instead of 3 cm.

quiz.q: An anthill is 3 cm south and 2 cm west of the ant. How long is the shortest grid route?

teach.ask: Gappu's friend ant walked 1 cm east, 2 cm north, then 1 cm west. Where is it compared with the start?
teach.praise: East 1 and west 1 cancel, so it is just 2 cm north of the start!
teach.nudge: What happens when you go 1 east and then 1 west?

learn.hook: The lion is at (3, 2) and the tiger at (2, 3). Are they in the same place? No! The order matters.
points: On a grid, a pair of numbers gives a position: the first number tells how far across, the second how far up.
(3, 2) means 3 across and 2 up. (2, 3) means 2 across and 3 up — a different spot!
To find the animal at a position, start at (0, 0), called the origin, go across, then up.
To write an animal's position, count across first, then up.
To plot a point, start at 0, move across, then up, and mark a dot.

example.q: Zoo grid: Lion (3, 2), Elephant (1, 4), Zebra (4, 1). Which animal is 1 across and 4 up?

learn.reallife: Seats in a cinema (row and number) and squares on a chessboard are found with pairs of letters or numbers too.

quiz.q: What does the position (3, 2) mean?
quiz.explain: The first number is across, the second is up.

quiz.q: Zoo grid: Lion (3, 2), Tiger (2, 3). Are they at the same place?
options: No, the order of numbers matters
Yes, if you turn the map
quiz.explain: 3 across 2 up is a different spot from 2 across 3 up.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the order does not matter

quiz.q: Lion (3, 2), Elephant (1, 4), Zebra (4, 1). Which animal is at 4 across, 1 up?
quiz.explain: (4, 1) is the zebra.

quiz.q: A peacock is 5 squares across and 2 squares up. How do you write its position?
quiz.explain: Across first, then up: (5, 2).

quiz.q: To plot (0, 4), where do you put the dot?
options: 4 straight up from the start, no moves across
quiz.explain: 0 across means stay on the up line; then 4 up.

quiz.q: The bear is at (2, 5). The deer is 3 squares to its right on the same row. Where is the deer?
quiz.explain: Moving right adds to the across number: 2 + 3 = 5. Up stays 5.

quiz.q: Which position is closest to the start (0, 0)?
quiz.explain: (1, 1) is only 2 squares of walking from the start along the lines.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the first number

quiz.q: Rhino at (4, 3) moves 2 squares up. What is its new position?
quiz.explain: Moving up adds to the second number: 3 + 2 = 5.

teach.ask: Gappu's nest is at (2, 4) on the zoo grid. How do I find it starting from (0, 0)?
teach.praise: Go 2 across first, then 4 up — there is my nest!
teach.nudge: Which number tells me to go across?

learn.hook: How can a whole state fit on one page? The secret is the map scale!
points: A map scale tells how much real distance 1 cm on the map stands for.
If 1 cm = 5 km, then 4 cm on the map is 4 × 5 = 20 km in real life.
Real distance = map length × the scale distance.
Map length = real distance ÷ the scale distance.
Always write the units: cm on the map, m or km in real life.

example.q: On a map, 1 cm stands for 5 km. Two towns are 4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?

learn.reallife: Road atlases, school plans and phone maps all use scales. Zooming in on a phone changes the scale!

items.q: 1 cm = 2 km. 10 km in real life = ? cm on the map

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 10 km. Two villages are 3 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
On Riya's school map, 1 cm = 100 m. The playground is 7 cm from the gate on the map. How far is it really?
quiz.mistake: Adds a zero too many or too few

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 2 km. Two towns are 12 km apart. How far apart are they on the map?
quiz.explain: Each 2 km takes 1 cm. 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

quiz.q: On Aisha's map, 1 cm = 50 km. Two cities are 4 cm apart. How far apart are they really?
A plan of a cricket ground uses 1 cm = 5 m. The ground is 9 cm long on the plan. How long is it really?
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Map A uses 1 cm = 1 km. Map B uses 1 cm = 2 km. Both show the same city on the same paper. On which map does the city look bigger?
quiz.explain: On Map A each km takes 1 cm. On Map B each km takes only half a cm. So the city looks bigger on Map A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger number in the scale makes things look bigger

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 25 km. A route has three parts of 2 cm, 3 cm and 1 cm on the map. How long is the real route?
quiz.explain: Total map length: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 cm. Real: 6 × 25 = 150 km.
quiz.mistake: Gives the map length in cm, or adds 25 only once

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 20 m. A park is 80 m wide. How wide is it on the map?

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can a big city fit on a small map? What is a scale?'
teach.praise: Clever! Each cm on the map stands for a real distance, so I multiply to find how far!
teach.nudge: What does 1 cm on the map stand for? How do I find the real distance?
